_about: The CLI, MCP and HTTP-API routes to the same functionality each use-case guide
shows in the portal. Documentation content, kept in the docs site rather than in
the e2e definitions, which describe only what a capture run executed.
Every entry is checked to EXIST by docs-site/scripts/check-usecase-surfaces.mjs,
against reference/cli.md, reference/mcp-tools.md and openapi.json — all three of
which are themselves generated from the product. So a renamed command fails the
docs build instead of quietly misleading a reader. What the check cannot prove is
that a command does what the surrounding page says; the pages state that.
An EMPTY list means the surface was searched and genuinely offers nothing — say
why in `notes`. A MISSING key means nobody has looked yet. The two render
differently, because they are different claims.

notes.mcp: MCP is reached with a token you already hold, so it has no sign-in tool of its own.
notes.api: `direct-login` exists for local development and is disabled unless ENABLE_DIRECT_LOGIN is set.
The query runs as the calling identity, so results are filtered by that identity's grants — the same rule the portal follows.
Creation is a PUT on the slug, and it is idempotent — the same request twice yields one workspace.

notes.mcp: No MCP tool manages service principals either — the portal and the HTTP API are the only two routes, so automation has to call the API.
No trigger tool is exposed to MCP.
notes.api: These are the ws-admin endpoints, which take an `X-Workspace` header. They are not the machine-facing `POST /triggers/{id}/events` endpoint a caller fires the trigger with — the portal's Connect dialog generates a worked example of that one.

notes.cli: `chameleon dbt run` runs a project that already exists. Creating the git connection and the project itself is the portal or the API.

notes.api: The kernel endpoint starts one for the workspace. A first start can fail and need retrying — the portal retries for you, a direct caller must.

notes.mcp: No MCP tool reads the audit trail. That is deliberate rather than missing: an assistant that can read every access record is a different risk from one that can read data it has been granted.
notes.api: Events are emitted in OCSF, the schema SIEM tools consume, so the forwarder feeds an existing pipeline rather than requiring a bespoke integration.
